title: Building for human evaluation: Spotting claims that go further than the quote
text: Because everything a reviewer would check by habit comes back clean. The claim says travel is reimbursed within 14 days. The cited document is real. The quoted sentence is in it word for word. And that sentence says 30 days. Every automatic check passes. The answer is still wrong and no stricter string matching anywhere would have caught it. It never attempts to decide whether the quote supports the claim and pretending otherwise would be the actual bug. So be precise about what a citation buys you. It proves the source exists. It proves the text was not invented. It does not prove the quote is relevant. It does not prove the claim follows from it. And it absolutely does not prove the answer is true. Build for the third check. It is the only one that decides whether the answer is true. Your turn. Here is the prompt. Take three answers my system produced with citations attached. For each one, quote the exact sentence from the source that supports it, then tell me whether that sentence actually says what the answer claims or only something nearby. Flag every case where the citation is real, but the claim goes further than the quote. Run that against your own output. The phrase to watch for is goes further than the quote because that is the failure that survives every automatic check you will ever write. That was grounding in retrieval.
